title: Authoritative Judicial Sources for Constitution 365
purpose: Authoritative source map for constitutional lessons requiring judicial interpretation, constitutional doctrine, judicial decisions or Supreme Court jurisprudence in addition to the constitutional text.

primary_authority: Constitution Bench judgments of the Supreme Court of India
rules: Do not present judicial interpretation as constitutional text.
Every case-specific proposition must be supported by a verified judgment.
Prefer Constitution Bench decisions for major constitutional doctrines.
Use the actual holding of the judgment and distinguish it from observations.
Do not invent case names, citations, dates, bench strength or holdings.
Do not use blogs, coaching material or secondary summaries as the primary authority.
Where a later judgment modifies or limits an earlier proposition, use the current legal position.
Judicial interpretation must remain distinguishable from statutory law and constitutional text.
A case source must exist in case_registry before it can be used by a doctrine.
Every judicial day must identify at least one applicable doctrine.
Every applicable doctrine must contain verified case sources.
Unresolved judicial sources must block generation.

supreme-court-of-india.description: Primary institutional source for Supreme Court judgments.

supreme-court-constitution-bench.description: Constitution Bench judgments concerning major constitutional questions.

kesavananda-bharati.case_name: His Holiness Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
kesavananda-bharati.issue: Extent of Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
kesavananda-bharati.holding: The power to amend the Constitution is subject to the basic-structure limitation.

maneka-gandhi.case_name: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
maneka-gandhi.issue: Meaning and scope of personal liberty and procedure under Article 21.
maneka-gandhi.holding: The procedure affecting personal liberty must satisfy constitutional standards of fairness and cannot be treated as a merely formal procedure.

minerva-mills.case_name: Minerva Mills Ltd v Union of India
minerva-mills.issue: Limits on constitutional amendment power and relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
minerva-mills.holding: Limited amending power and judicial review form part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

bandhua-mukti-morcha.case_name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v Union of India
bandhua-mukti-morcha.issue: Enforcement of fundamental rights of vulnerable and bonded labourers through public interest proceedings.
bandhua-mukti-morcha.holding: The Court recognised a broad approach to Article 32 proceedings in matters involving serious violations of fundamental rights of disadvantaged persons.

hussainara-khatoon.case_name: Hussainara Khatoon v Home Secretary, State of Bihar
hussainara-khatoon.issue: Prolonged detention of undertrial prisoners and speedy trial.
hussainara-khatoon.holding: Speedy trial was recognised as an important component of the protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21.

dk-basu.case_name: D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal
dk-basu.issue: Safeguards against custodial violence and abuse during arrest and detention.
dk-basu.holding: The Court laid down safeguards concerning arrest and detention to protect constitutional rights and prevent custodial abuse.

nilabati-behera.case_name: Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
nilabati-behera.issue: Public-law remedy for violation of life and personal liberty.
nilabati-behera.holding: Constitutional courts may grant public-law compensation for established violations of fundamental rights.

sr-bommai.case_name: S.R. Bommai v Union of India
sr-bommai.issue: Constitutional limits and judicial review concerning President's Rule.
sr-bommai.holding: The exercise of power under Article 356 is subject to constitutional limitations and judicial review.

l-chandra-kumar.case_name: L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India
l-chandra-kumar.issue: Judicial review by constitutional courts and the role of tribunals.
l-chandra-kumar.holding: Judicial review by the Supreme Court under Article 32 and High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 is part of the Constitution's basic structure.

vishaka.issue: Protection against sexual harassment at the workplace in the absence of an adequate statutory framework.
vishaka.holding: The Court issued binding guidelines to protect constitutional rights in a legislative vacuum.

ec-il-karunakar.case_name: Managing Director, ECIL, Hyderabad v B. Karunakar
ec-il-karunakar.holding: Failure to provide the inquiry report in the circumstances addressed by the Court can violate principles of natural justice and fair procedure.

supreme-court-bar-association.case_name: Supreme Court Bar Association v Union of India
supreme-court-bar-association.issue: Scope of the Supreme Court's contempt power and Article 142.
supreme-court-bar-association.holding: Article 142 cannot be used to assume powers that belong to another constitutional or statutory authority contrary to the constitutional scheme.

supreme-court-aor-association.case_name: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v Union of India
supreme-court-aor-association.holding: The National Judicial Appointments Commission framework was held unconstitutional, with judicial independence treated as a fundamental constitutional principle.

ir-coelho.case_name: I.R. Coelho v State of Tamil Nadu
ir-coelho.issue: Judicial review of laws placed in the Ninth Schedule.
ir-coelho.holding: Constitutional amendments placing laws in the Ninth Schedule after the relevant constitutional developments remain subject to basic-structure review where fundamental rights forming part of the basic structure are affected.

shreya-singhal.case_name: Shreya Singhal v Union of India
shreya-singhal.issue: Freedom of speech and restrictions on online expression.
shreya-singhal.holding: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was held unconstitutional for violating freedom of speech and expression.

puttaswamy-privacy.case_name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India
puttaswamy-privacy.holding: Privacy is a constitutionally protected right arising from the guarantees of dignity, liberty and other fundamental rights.

navtej-singh-johar.case_name: Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India
navtej-singh-johar.issue: Constitutional protection of dignity, equality and individual autonomy.
navtej-singh-johar.holding: Constitutional rights protect dignity, equality and individual autonomy, and constitutional morality has an important role in rights adjudication.

joseph-shine.case_name: Joseph Shine v Union of India
joseph-shine.holding: The Court invalidated the adultery offence framework as unconstitutional, emphasising equality, dignity and individual autonomy.

national-legal-services-authority.case_name: National Legal Services Authority v Union of India
national-legal-services-authority.issue: Equality, dignity and constitutional protection of transgender persons.
national-legal-services-authority.holding: The Court recognised constitutional equality, dignity and protection for transgender persons.

sharad-birdhi-chand-sarda.case_name: Sharad Birdhi Chand Sarda v State of Maharashtra
sharad-birdhi-chand-sarda.issue: Criminal adjudication and assessment of evidence.
sharad-birdhi-chand-sarda.holding: The Court laid down principles concerning evaluation of circumstantial evidence in criminal cases.

abhiram-singh.issue: Corrupt electoral practices involving appeals on grounds of religion, race, caste, community or language.
abhiram-singh.holding: Section 123(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 was interpreted to prohibit appeals on the specified identity grounds in the electoral context.

electoral-bonds.case_name: Association for Democratic Reforms v Union of India
electoral-bonds.issue: Constitutionality of the Electoral Bond Scheme and disclosure of political funding information.
electoral-bonds.holding: The Electoral Bond Scheme and related statutory amendments were held unconstitutional in the judgment of 15 February 2024, including on the basis of citizens' right to information regarding political funding.

keshavananda-election-basic-structure.case_name: Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain
keshavananda-election-basic-structure.issue: Constitutional amendment and adjudication of election disputes.
keshavananda-election-basic-structure.holding: The Court applied the basic-structure limitation to invalidate constitutional provisions affecting the judicial determination of election disputes.

common-cause.case_name: Common Cause v Union of India
common-cause.issue: Right to life, dignity and end-of-life decision-making.
common-cause.holding: The Court recognised dimensions of the right to die with dignity within Article 21 subject to the constitutional and legal safeguards laid down by the Court.

validation.generation_rule: A judicial lesson may be generated only when its day is verified, every declared doctrine exists, every doctrine is verified and every case source exists in case_registry.
validation.unresolved_source_rule: Any judicial day or doctrine marked unresolved must block generation.
validation.case_registry_rule: A case must not be referenced by a doctrine unless it exists in case_registry.
validation.precedent_rule: Where later authoritative precedent changes the legal position, the current position must be used.
validation.source_distinction_rule: Judicial holdings must never be presented as literal constitutional or statutory text.
